correctness.rationale: The two published exact sharp frame-bound expressions reduce after dividing by 2n to Fminus=e^-x tanh(t/2) x csch(x) and Fplus=e^x coth(t/2) x csch(x), x=t/n. Their logarithmic derivatives give the exact stationary equations (7.9) and (7.10). Uniform expansions around L=log(2n) locate the distinct unique extrema at signed L/(3n)+O(L^2/n^2). The exact ratio optimizer is arsinh(n). Direct twice-differentiated expansions give Fminus second derivative -1/n+O(L/n^2) and Fplus +1/n+O(L/n^2), yielding two relative regrets asymptotic to L^2/(18n^3). Dilation eliminates the window-rate parameter; the finite checker is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The published one-sided Gabor frame theorem shows that optimal lower bound, upper bound, and conditioning require distinct rectangular lattices, posing a natural simultaneous design/calibration tradeoff. The new all-large-n sharp split O(log n/n) and equal normalized losses log^2 n/(18n^3) quantify precisely when one choice becomes asymptotically near-optimal for both frame edges. These are meaningful whole-family asymptotics rather than a finite numerical slice or a renamed inequality.
